newsitem.title: UK: Animal feed demand seen up if UK cold persists.
newsitem.headline: Animal feed demand seen up if UK cold persists.

text.p: UK animal feed demand is likely to rise if current cold weather persists, feed trade sources said.

But the effect will not be as great as it once would have been. Improved livestock keeping practice and higher investment have made farmers less dependent on extra feed to get stock through the winter.
"Farmers have had lots of money thrown at them in the last few years and they've put some of it back into sheds and heaters and general husbandry," a feed compounder said.
He could see some small impact already.
"There has been a definite increase in take-off in the last few days," the compounder said. But others were less sure.
"There's been no increase in movements of grain in the last few days," a grain trader said.
Impact is small so far but could increase if cold persists.
"It will be pushing some people's purchases up," a feed industry analyst said. But he pointed out that the East of England was most hit by the cold while livestock farmers tend to be in the West.

He noted that the winter had not yet produced big snowdrifts which have forced farmers to airlift feed to stock in some areas in past years. If the cold were to last 10 more days it could start to have a more severe impact on feed use, he said.
The cold is not causing any big problems for cereals producers, farming sources said.
"If anything it's not a bad thing," a sector analyst said, as it was likely to mean crop development did not go too fast.

Europe's New Year freeze is set to continue until at least early next week with temperatures likely to remain below normal for this time of year over the next six to 10 days, a private weather forecaster said on Friday.
"A severe cold wave continues as the predominant wind flow is from the east," U.S. Weather Services Corp (WSC) said.
